item.text: A new monotonicity edge emerges from the sync path: a late follower can legally have a higher decided index than the new leader’s current committed index, yet `sync_log` assigns the leader’s lower index unconditionally. I’m testing whether synchronization can move a follower’s decided index backward.

item.text:
The audit now has 26 confirmed findings. This pass added a core synchronization defect:

- **`AcceptSync` can move a follower’s decided index backward.** A receiver that had decided through index 10 accepted a valid sync carrying the new leader’s decided index 5 and regressed to 5. Entries 6–10 remained present but disappeared from the public decided view, violating monotonic decided visibility: [audit_sync_decided_regression.rs](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_22-19-35-omnipaxos-baseline/work/omnipaxos/tests/audit_sync_decided_regression.rs).

The snapshot-aware crash harness also reproduced a decided/snapshot conflict at step 50, independently corroborating the delta-snapshot defect.

The highest-impact findings now include multiple `sync_log` correctness issues, persistent failed-write state leakage, LFU clone corruption, timeout retry duplication, and LRU bincode deserialization failure. Complete evidence is in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_22-19-35-omnipaxos-baseline/work/report.md).
